messages.text: Can read the CMS Tracker TDR first, to gather two inputs from the RD53 usage - before we move on ?
I’ll give the CMS Tracker TDR the same extraction and broad reading pass, with a map of its RD53-related sections. That will give us both ATLAS and CMS inputs before the focused module-evidence work.

The CMS extraction is complete: 353 pages. One important distinction is already clear: the TDR discusses RD53A as a planned demonstrator, so its projected readout-chip requirements must stay separate from the later RD53A manual’s specifications. I’m recording that distinction alongside the CMS module and services references.

The CMS pass adds useful module-level context: chip tiling, the flex circuit and base strips, serial powering, and the transition from electrical to optical links. I also found inconsistent planned submission dates for RD53A within the TDR; the guide will flag these as historical plans and keep them out of any design assumptions.

The CMS guide and cross-source reading routes are now written. The 353-page cache passes the page-coverage and retrieval checks, and the documentation/logging tests pass. I’m finishing the session record; the next pass can compare ATLAS and CMS module choices against the shared RD53A reference.

Done: extracted all **353 pages** and read the CMS passages on RD53, module construction, powering and services.

- [CMS reading guide](reference/guides/SRC-CMS-TDR-014.md) records exact locators and caveats.
- [Cross-source routes](reference/guides/README.md) now connect **ATLAS + CMS + RD53A**.
- Updated provenance, ADR-005’s draft scope, PR description and session log.

Key distinction: CMS’s target-chip requirements differ from the RD53A demonstrator specifications. The guide preserves that distinction.

**Checks:** four retrieval checks, 15 documentation/logging tests and validation of all seven session records passed.

Changes remain uncommitted on `m0/reference-reading-pilot`. Ready for the focused comparison; no detector parameters adopted.
